findings.title: U.S. Spy Agencies Suffer Breach of Some Unclassified Information
findings.summary_md: The New York Times first reported that the CIA and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence discovered a cybersecurity breach that exposed some unclassified information. The report said the intrusions affected a network used to find intelligence insights in public, unclassified material. It was not clear which material was compromised, and the Times said information at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed.

findings.title: US CIA, ODNI suffer cybersecurity breach of some unclassified information, source says
findings.summary_md: Reuters reported that the CIA and ODNI recently discovered a breach exposing some unclassified information, citing a person familiar with the matter. The intrusions affected a network that looks for intelligence insights in public, unclassified material, according to the New York Times. ODNI said there had been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems. Reuters noted that information at other government agencies was also believed to have been exposed.

findings.title: CIA and ODNI discover breach exposing some unclassified information, NYT reports
findings.summary_md: CTV News carried Reuters reporting that the CIA and ODNI discovered a breach exposing some unclassified information. The affected network was used to search public, unclassified material for intelligence insights, and the specific material compromised was not identified. The report placed the incident alongside other recent government cyber incidents and technology outages.

findings.title: CIA hit by hack impacting unclassified information
findings.summary_md: CNN reported, citing four sources familiar with the matter, that the CIA and ODNI suffered an apparent hack affecting unclassified information on a system used for open-source intelligence analysis. An ODNI official said there had been no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems. CNN said it was not clear when the hack occurred, who was responsible or whether it had been resolved, and that the incident did not appear related to the apparent hack of the FBI nationwide criminal information database. The report noted that ODNI oversees 17 US intelligence agencies.
